short: The first military heavier-than-air aircraft, pioneering the concept of military aviation.
full:
In August 1909, the United States Army Signal Corps formally accepted the Wright Military Flyer following successful trials at Fort Myer, Virginia. Purchased for $30,000, it became the world's first military aeroplane, designated Signal Corps Airplane No. 1. While unarmed and relatively fragile, its ability to carry a pilot and passenger at speeds exceeding forty miles per hour demonstrated that heavier-than-air flight had practical utility beyond mere exhibition.

The aircraft served for almost two years, primarily as a training platform. Lieutenants Frank P. Lahm, Frederick E. Humphreys, and Benjamin Foulois used it to become the first military aviators, mastering the Wright brothers' complex control system. Although rapidly superseded by more capable designs and retired by April 1911, the Military Flyer established the foundation for army aviation and irrevocably altered the trajectory of modern warfare.
